caption: The drawing shows a rectangular woven textile pattern composed of repeating geometric shapes and colors. The main colors in the pattern are blue, orange, and beige. The beige forms the base grid structure, with vertical and horizontal bands of orange and blue. The blue sections are made up of closely spaced blue squares and rectangles grouped together to form larger squares and oval-like shapes set within the grid. The orange sections consist of several horizontal rows of rectangles with lighter, thin horizontal lines crossing through them, creating a textured appearance. The orange and blue colored shapes alternate and align both vertically and horizontally, creating a regular, repeating pattern across the entire textile. The grid lines consisting of thin beige lines intersect throughout the design, separating the colored sections into distinct, well-defined blocks. The whole pattern is set against a plain off-white background with a thin border of the same color around the textile. Near the bottom right corner, there is a small signature reading "Christoffels."
title: Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
